subject: Secondary replicas / backup retention — DPA language and proofing
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@cloudedge.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudEdge Legal <legal@cloudedge.com>, procurement@cloudedge.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Questions: DPA retention for secondary replicas / backups

Hi Michael —

Thanks for the call earlier. As we prepare the DPA redline with our legal team, we need clarification on a few points around backups and secondary replicas so we can finalize our retention and deletion language. Specific asks below: 

1) Backup retention cascade: if customer data is deleted (customer requests erasure), what is the expected timeline for removal from primary, secondary replicas, and off-site backup snapshots? Please list typical windows and any exceptions.

2) Onshore copies: you previously mentioned regional snapshots for DR. Can we get language committing to the region of backups for CloudEdge EU customers (we're focusing on US/US-EU for this deal)?

3) Proof of deletion: do you provide a deletion certificate or manifest for wiped data (including snapshots)? If so, what metadata is included (timestamp, storage ID, snapshot id, operator id)?

4) Backup immutability / legal hold: how are legal holds handled with respect to backups? Can a legal hold extend retention beyond the standard deletion cascade, and how is this surfaced to the customer?

5) Recovery windows: what is the expected maximum time between a deletion request being accepted and all customer-accessible copies being unrecoverable? We want a reasonably short SLA here or at least a documented process.

If you can provide suggested redline wording for the DPA (we're starting from your standard DPA) that addresses the above points, it would speed review. Also attaching a short timeline that our infra team expects for map — happy to take your counterproposal.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Cloud Security, CloudEdge Inc.
elena@cloudedge.com

[attachment: timeline_expectations.pdf (pdf)]

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cloudedge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions: DPA retention for secondary replicas / backups

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. I've looped in Laura (Legal) and Jordan (Ops) — answers and a proposed DPA snippet below. I've attached a first-pass redline (DPA_redline_v1.docx) and a simple data flow diagram to show where snapshots/replicas live.

High-level answers (we'll put these into contract language):

- Typical cascade windows: primary delete propagation starts immediately. In practice: tombstone/metadata purge from primary within 24–72 hours; secondary replicas (cross-AZ) reconcile within 72 hours; immutable backup snapshots (scheduled daily incremental) are retained according to the configured snapshot TTL — default 30 days for hosted customers. Restoration-capable snapshots are retained until TTL expiry; upon TTL expiration snapshots are garbage-collected within 7 calendar days.

- Onshore copies: we support regional snapshot placement. For EU customers we can commit to storing production backups within EU regions and to maintain EU-only onshore replicas for backups required by the contract. Suggested clause: "Backups and disaster-recovery replicas for Customer data designated EU shall be stored within EU data centers and shall not be transferred outside the EU without Customer's prior written consent."

- Proof of deletion: we can issue a deletion manifest that includes: snapshot id, storage bucket (region), deletion timestamp, and the job id that triggered the deletion. We do not include operator PII in manifests, but we can include an operator id token. We'll propose: "Upon Customer request Redwood will produce an auditable Deletion Manifest containing the identifiers of deleted snapshots/replicas, timestamps, and verification job ids."

- Legal hold: Legal holds are honored and will prevent GC/irreversible deletion of backups. We will surface holds via the Console API and provide notice to the customer. Proposed: "Legal holds placed by Customer will supersede standard TTLs and Redwood will not expire or purge data subject to an active legal hold; Redwood will provide metadata evidence of holds and scopes to Customer upon request."

- Recovery windows / SLA: for hosted customers we can commit to a process: deletion request acknowledged within 24 hours; primary metadata purge within 72 hours; backup snapshot GC complete within 30 days (for default TTLs) unless accelerated by an agreed-on escrowing/expedited removal process. For Dedicated / Private deployments we can offer shorter windows by config/ops agreement.

Attached is DPA_redline_v1.docx with suggested language and a brief callout of where we need procurement/legal signoff for onshore backup commitments. Jordan — can you confirm the 7-day GC window after TTL expiry (this is about background GC jobs)?

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com

Attachments: DPA_redline_v1.docx (docx), data_flow_diagram.png (png)

From: Elena Morales <elena@cloudedge.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudEdge Legal <legal@cloudedge.com>, procurement@cloudedge.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions: DPA retention for secondary replicas / backups

Thanks — that is helpful but CloudEdge Legal has two follow-ups before we can accept the proposed wording: 

1) Proof of deletion detail: the deletion manifest needs to include a machine-verifiable digest (hash) of the snapshot contents or manifest id that maps to an immutable log entry (we need tamper-evidence). Is Redwood able to provide a checksum or an immutable log entry id tied to deletion jobs?

2) Accelerated deletion option: CloudEdge wants an option to request an expedited GC for specific snapshots (e.g., within 7 days of request) with an associated admin/ops contact and a one-time fee if operationally required. We also want clarity on what qualifies as "legal hold" vs "operational hold" and how those are communicated.

3) Documentation: please provide an example deletion manifest and a redline that includes the onshore backup sentence. Our legal team flagged the phrase "without Customer's prior written consent" as too weak — they prefer "without Customer's prior written consent except where required by applicable law" (i.e., to allow legal process).

If you can supply DPA_redline_v2 with the checksum/manifest sample and a proposed operational escalation path (contact + expected time to start accelerated GC), that will move us forward. Also please include a short appendix showing the audit log fields that will be available in the manifest.

Best,
Elena

Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions: DPA retention for secondary replicas / backups

Elena —

Thanks for the feedback and the specificity from your legal team. We've updated the redline per your asks and added an example Deletion Manifest template in the appendix of DPA_redline_v2.docx. Summary of changes and commitments below: 

- Tamper-evidence: We'll include a SHA-256 digest of the snapshot manifest in the Deletion Manifest and store the manifest in an append-only audit log (internal id + timestamp). The Deletion Manifest will reference the audit log id so you can correlate deletion events to immutable entries. New contract language: "Redwood will produce a Deletion Manifest referencing an append-only audit log entry and including a SHA-256 digest of the snapshot manifest to provide tamper-evident proof of deletion."

- Accelerated deletion: We will offer an "Expedited GC" option: upon written Customer request Redwood will begin an accelerated garbage collection process targeting specified snapshots with a target completion of 7 calendar days from request (subject to operational constraints). There is a one-time operational fee for expedited removal for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private will be handled under the service contract. Operational escalation path: ops-oncall@redwood.com (24x7) and security-ops@redwood.com (business hours).

- Onshore backup wording: revised per your suggestion to include lawful exception: "Backups and disaster-recovery replicas for Customer data designated EU shall be stored within EU data centers and shall not be transferred outside the EU without Customer's prior written consent except where required by applicable law or judicial process."

- Example manifest fields (appendix): snapshot_id, snapshot_digest (SHA-256), region, bucket/path, deletion_timestamp, audit_log_entry_id, gc_job_id, manifest_version. We've added a sample JSON manifest in the appendix.

Next steps: I've uploaded DPA_redline_v2.docx which contains the exact redline (and the sample manifest). I've also created the DocuSign envelope for the updated DPA and shared the link below. If those items look good, please sign and we'll queue the expedited GC run if you request it after signing.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/CE-2026-0011
HubSpot: 2345678

Would you like a short sync (20 min) on Monday to walk legal through the manifest and the expedited-GC mechanics?

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com
